title: Neuroprojection

context.description: Traditional brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) focus on control and diagnosis, creating a clinical distance between the user and their neural data. This approach misses the opportunity for personal reflection and aesthetic experience. The intent is to create an immersive, non-diagnostic experience where participants can witness their brainwave activity as a living, evolving visual environment.
keyPoints: Moves beyond clinical BCI applications to focus on personal reflection
Creates an aesthetic experience from neural data
Encourages personal interpretation rather than diagnosis
Serves as a mirror for self-observation and awareness

systemOverview.description: EEG signals are captured in real-time, processed through frequency analysis, and mapped to visual parameters.
flow: EEG headset captures raw brainwave signals
Signal processing extracts frequency bands (Alpha, Beta, Theta, Delta, Gamma)
Frequency data maps to visual parameters (color, motion, scale, complexity)
Real-time rendering engine generates projected environment
Participant observes and reflects on the visual feedback

mappings.visual: Flowing, organic forms; cool blues and greens; gentle motion
Structured, geometric patterns; warm oranges and reds; rapid movement
Deep, layered textures; purples and indigos; slow, undulating motion
Minimal, sparse forms; dark tones; near-stillness
High-frequency patterns; bright whites and yellows; rapid oscillations

participantExperience: Participants sit in a dimly lit space, wearing a comfortable EEG headset. As they close their eyes, breathe, or simply observe their thoughts, the projected environment responds in real-time. There is no instruction manual—only the invitation to notice. The experience is personal, non-judgmental, and open to interpretation. After 10-15 minutes, participants are invited to reflect on what they observed, though no data is recorded or analyzed.
